statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 13%, inside the low band and below the watch threshold.
recommendation: Conditions describe a completed and orderly trend-up cash session followed by a quiet, two-sided Globex reopen. NQ is trading 29,490.00 inside a 27-point 29,482.00-29,509.00 band, the cash index settled about 56 points below its high, and volatility decayed into the close with VIX at 14.32. The near checkpoints are the Asian open and the European open at 07:00Z. The single narrow danger window is the 12:30-14:00Z August employment report on 4 September, which lands before a three-day U.S. weekend.
headline: Quiet two-sided Globex reopen with NQ at 29,490.00 after the Nasdaq-100 settled 29,482.32 (+1.16%) and September hike odds fell to roughly even
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,482.32, up 1.16%, inside a 29,160.96-29,538.76 range, finishing about 56 points below the session high rather than pinned to it. Globex reopened at 22:00Z and the first prints are two-sided: NQ 29,490.00, down 0.12% against the settle, inside a 27-point 29,482.00-29,509.00 band. That combination, a completed advance that already retraced before the settle plus a range-bound reopen, is why Tail eases to 13% despite an unambiguous trend-up cash session. The driver of the session was policy repricing. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said he would be inclined to support holding the target range at the 15-16 September meeting if disinflation continues, and CME FedWatch odds of a September hike fell to 50.4% from 63.2%. The 2-year yield eased to about 4.35% and the 10-year to about 4.77%, both off the multi-year high touched earlier in the week, helped by a roughly 2% stronger yen near 155.36. Breadth was broad rather than narrow: the Dow added 1.18% to 53,686.11, the S&P 500 1.06% to 7,747.71 and the Nasdaq Composite 1.40% to 26,584.06, and the ISM services index came in at 55.4 against a 54.1 consensus. Delayed cross-asset context shows seven of eight Nasdaq megacaps higher on the session, while semiconductors were split four to three with Broadcom down about 2.7% on guidance despite an earnings beat, so the advance was not a single narrow leadership stack. VIX finished 14.32, down 5.79%, near its 14.23 session low, which is volatility decay rather than expansion. After the close, single-name earnings reactions were idiosyncratic and did not produce index-level direction. The unresolved item remains energy: WTI near $91.75 and Brent near $95.75 with Iran continuing strikes on U.S. Gulf allies and Brent up roughly 30% since the conflict began. That keeps Stress in the low 50s without establishing an equity-index price path that denies retracement. Forward risk is concentrated in one narrow window: the August employment report at 12:30Z on 4 September, with survey consensus clustered near +42K to +58K payrolls and the unemployment rate seen holding at 4.1%, followed by the 13:30Z cash open. Consistent with prior calibration, event magnitude and forecast dispersion raise Stress and lower Confidence across those hours rather than asserting that a no-retracement path has already formed, so the projected Tail is capped at the top of the watch band through the release and the cash open and decays quickly thereafter if price discovery proves orderly.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the published state was green in 19 of the 22 assessed hours. Tail sat between 11% and 14% through the late US evening, the Asian session and the European morning while Stress drifted from the mid 50s down to 52%. The state moved to yellow at 15:00Z and 16:00Z with Tail at 21% and 20% as the index held its session extreme after the Waller remarks and the ISM services beat, returned to green at 17:00Z during consolidation, went yellow again at 18:00Z on a fresh session high, then back to green from 19:00Z once that high was retraced and the index settled below it, with Tail easing to 14% by 21:00Z. Two hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The near path keeps Tail in the low band now that Globex has reopened two-sided and the cash session has settled below its high, easing to an overnight floor of 12% through the Asian session as participation thins. Risk rebuilds gradually across European hours into the August employment report at 12:30Z on 4 September, which is the mapped danger window through 14:00Z. Tail is deliberately capped at the top of the watch band across the release hour and the US cash open that follows, because event magnitude and forecast dispersion raise Stress and lower Confidence rather than establishing a no-retracement price path. Beyond 14:00Z the projection assumes orderly price discovery and decay back into the low band, with a small Stress rebuild into the Friday close to reflect three-day weekend gap exposure while the Iran-Gulf energy file is unresolved.
